title: Food Safety and Allergen Standard
elements:
Food Safety and Allergen Standard
Version 4. Effective June 1, 2026. Owner: Quality and Food Safety Manager. Approved by the
Leadership Team on May 11, 2026. Replaces version 3.
1 Scope
This standard applies to every café and to the roastery's tasting room. It covers how milk, food, and
prepared drink ingredients are stored and held, temperature checks, allergens, handwashing, and
when a sick employee stays home. Where the local health code is stricter, follow the health code.
2 Holding temperatures and times
Cold items are held at 41°F (5°C) or below, and hot items at 135°F (57°C) or above. Label every
opened or prepared item with the date and time it was opened or made, and throw it out when its time
runs out.

3 Heating sandwiches
Heat breakfast sandwiches in the oven to an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C), checked with a
probe thermometer, before they go in the warmer. Record one probe reading per batch on the
temperature log. A sandwich that drops below 135°F (57°C) in the warmer is thrown out, not reheated.

4 Fridge and freezer checks
Read every fridge and freezer thermometer at opening, at 2:00 p.m., and at close, and record the
readings on the temperature log. Freezers read 0°F (-18°C) or below. If a fridge reads above 41°F
(5°C), check it again after 30 minutes. If it's still above 41°F (5°C), move everything to another fridge,
call the Facilities help desk, and tell the Café Manager. Throw out any milk or food that has been above
41°F (5°C) for more than 4 hours, or for an unknown length of time.
5 Allergens
5.1 What we track
Halcyon tracks the nine major allergens: milk, eggs, fish, shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soy, and
sesame. Almond milk and the hazelnut and pistachio syrups contain tree nuts. Oat milk is not certified
gluten-free. Each pastry's allergens are printed on its label and listed in the allergen binder.
5.2 Making an allergy order
When a guest mentions an allergy, add the ALLERGY modifier in the register so it prints on the cup
label. The barista making the drink washes their hands, takes a pitcher from the clean rack, purges and
wipes the steam wand before steaming, and uses the purple allergen-safe blender jar for blended
drinks. Tell the guest that our cafés handle all nine allergens and we can't promise any item is free of
them.
5.3 If a guest has a reaction
Call 911 if the guest has trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or feels faint. Don't give the
guest any medication, though they may use their own epinephrine injector. Tell the Café Manager, keep
the cup and any packaging, and file an incident report in the safety portal within 24 hours.
6 Handwashing and gloves
Wash your hands for at least 20 seconds at the start of each shift, after breaks, after handling raw eggs,
cash, or trash, and before putting on gloves. Wear gloves to handle ready-to-eat food that won't be
cooked. Change gloves every 4 hours, and whenever they tear or you change tasks.
7 Illness
An employee with vomiting, diarrhea, or jaundice doesn't work until 48 hours after the symptoms stop.
An employee with a sore throat and a fever works only away from food and drinks, such as on the
register, until the fever is gone. Tell the person in charge before the shift; paid sick time covers the
missed shifts.
